source.excerpt: Visible light-mediated selective amidation of unactivated \mathrm { C } ( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 } ) \mathrm { - H } bonds is presented with acyl sulfilimines as free nitrene precursors via triplet<sup>–</sup>triplet energy transfer pathway. Both intermolecular and intramolecular reactions were achieved under mild, additive-free conditions without metal<sup>–</sup>nitrenoids formed. This protocol offers a widely applicable approach to access various synthetically versatile compounds, including N-acyl hemiaminal ether, benzo[e][1,3]oxazin-4-one, and isoindolin-1-one derivatives in a selective manner.

We began our investigation using dibenzothiophene-based N-benzoyl sulfilimine (1a) as the nitrene precursor, Ir[dF(CF ) \mathrm { p p y } ] _ { 2 } ( \mathrm { d t b b p y } ) \mathrm { P F } _ { 6 } (1 mol%) as the photocatalyst and THF (0.1 M) as the C<sup>–</sup>H donor under blue light emitting diode (LED) irradiation. Excitingly, the desired \mathrm { C } ( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 } ) – \mathrm { H } amidation product 2a was obtained selectively in 76% yield after 3 h (Table 1, entry 1). Changing the photocatalyst to \operatorname { I r } ( \mathrm { d F p p y } ) _ { 3 } gave a slightly lower yield of 61%, while fac-Ir(ppy) and Mes- \mathrm { { A c r } ^ { + } \mathrm { { C l } \mathrm { { O } _ { 4 } ^ { - } } } } resulted in only a trace amount of 2a (Table 1, entries 2<sup>–</sup>4). Other aromatic ketone-type photocatalysts could also promote this reaction, providing 2a in 19%<sup>–</sup>66% yields (Table 1, entries 5 and ^ { 6 , } also see Table S1). Not surprisingly, no product 2a was formed in the absence of the catalyst or light (Table 1, entries 7 and 8).

To gain more insight into the \mathrm { C } ( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 } ) – \mathrm { H } amidation, a series of mechanistic experiments were conducted. First, when the reaction of 1a with THF was performed in the presence of TEMPO (2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidinyloxy), the amidated product 2a was not observed. Instead, adducts 8, 9, and 10 were obtained, indicating the formation of a free triplet nitrene intermediate and the possibility of a hydrogen atom abstraction (HAA) process (Scheme 4A) [47, 48]. Reaction of 1a with the styrene under standard conditions gave the corresponding dihydrooxazole 11 in 37% yield, which further confirmed the generation of an acylnitrene intermediate (Scheme 4B) [49]. Control experiments revealed that in the absence of a photocatalyst, 1a underwent Curtius-like rearrangement and following hydrolysis to form N, N<sup>’</sup>-diphenyl urea 2a<sup>’</sup> in 21% yield without 2a formed (Scheme 4C) [50]. Applying 370 nm light irradiation instead of blue light gave 14% of 2a and 34% of 2a<sup>’</sup>, which is in accordance with the UV/Vis absorption of 1a (see Figure S1). Stern<sup>–</sup>Volmer quenching experiments showed that 1a quenched the photocatalyst \mathrm { I r [ d F ( C F _ { 3 } ) p p y ] _ { 2 } ( d t b b p y ) P F _ { 6 } } efficiently (Scheme 4D). To prove the role of photocatalyst in the reaction, we evaluated a

wide range of photosensitizers varying in triplet-state energy ( E _ { \mathrm { T } } ) and redox properties (Scheme 4E). As a result, the reaction is believed to initiate with a triplet<sup>–</sup>triplet energy transfer (EnT) rather than electron transfer since the yield of 2a correlates to E _ { \mathrm { T } } of photocatalysts but is unrelated to redox characteristics (see Table S6). Moreover, our previous work showed that there is no obvious reduction peak of 1a in the cyclic voltammetry measurements [51]. The E _ { \mathrm { T } } of 1a was found to be 62.0 kcal/mol by density functional theory calculations (see Table S7), which closely matched that of the photocatalyst. Furthermore, the deuterium kinetic isotope effect (KIE) was performed and the intermolecular competition experiment resulted in a KIE k _ { \mathrm { H } } / k _ { \mathrm { D } } of 1.3, suggesting that the hydrogen transfer may not be the rate-determining step (Scheme 4F). In light of these results, a plausible mechanism is proposed in Scheme 4G. Upon visible light irradiation, an EnT process from the excited \mathrm { I r } [ \mathrm { d F } ( \mathrm { C F } _ { 3 } ) \mathrm { p p y } ] _ { 2 } ( \mathrm { d t b b p y } ) \mathrm { P F } _ { 6 } to sulfilimines gives the excited state 1*, which forms a triplet nitrene 1-I on releasing dibenzothiophene. The intermediate 1-I can then engage in HAA process with THF to deliver an α-oxo radical A as well as an amide radical 1-II, followed by radical rebound to furnish the final product.

Zhe Jin and Xia Liu conducted most experiments and prepared the SI. Lu Kang, Xinyu Lu, and Tingwei Yu contributed to part of the substrate scope investigation. Penghao Jia designed and directed the project.

Sulfilimine 1 (0.1 mmol, 1.0 equiv.) and \mathrm { I r ( d F ( C F _ { 3 } ) p p y ) _ { 2 } ( d t b b p y ) P F _ { 6 } } (1.1 mg, 1.0 mol%) were dissolved in THF (1.0 mL, 0.1 M) in a 10 mL dry reaction tube. Plug the test tube with a rubber stopper and bubble the reaction solution with a nitrogen gas balloon for 10 min. The mixture was allowed to stir under 36 W blue LEDs irradiation at room temperature for 3 h and monitored through TLC analysis. The crude product was directly separated and purified on 2 0 0 \ast 2 0 0 mm thin layer silica gel plate ( \mathrm { P E } ; \mathrm { E A } = 2 ; 1 \sim 1 ; 1 ) to obtain the desired product 2 as a white solid.

Visible luminescence intensity was recorded using an Instruments F - 4700FL spectrophotometer. All luminescence measurements were recorded using a micro quartz cuvette. All \mathrm { I r [ d F ( C F _ { 3 } ) p p y ] _ { 2 } ( d t b b p y ) P F _ { 6 } } solutions were excited at 380 nm and the emission intensity at 470 nm was observed. All solutions of the mixture of sulifilimine 1a with \mathrm { I r [ d F ( C F _ { 3 } ) p p y ] _ { 2 } ( d t b b p y ) P F _ { 6 } } were dissolved in acetonitrile.
5.8 DFT Calculations
5.8.1 General

Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were carried out with the Gaussian16 program package. Unrestricted DFT was used to optimize geometries of the lowest triplet state \left( \mathrm { T } _ { 1 } \right) . With the optimized geometries were calculated using PBE0 levels of theory with 6-311g(d) basis set and the IEFPCM model to consider solvent effects (acetonitrile), single point energies were calculated using PBE0 levels of theory with def2-TZVP basis set and the SMD model to consider solvent effects (acetonitrile). Vibrational frequency calculations were performed at the same level as the geometry optimizations to confirm all optimized structures as minima (no imaginary frequency). The singlepoint energies were converted to Gibbs free energies at 298 K in the solvent by the addition of gasphase thermal correction to Gibbs free energy obtained from the frequency analysis. The radii of molecules were obtained by calculating molecular volume. Optimized structures were illustrated using CYLView.

All experiments were performed in oven-dried glassware under nitrogen unless otherwise stated. All reagents were purchased from Heowns, Bidepharm, Aladdin, Macklin and Leyan, and used without further purification unless otherwise noted. Thin-layer chromatography (TLC) analysis of reaction mixtures was performed on 0.20-0.25 mm silica gel GF254 plates (HaiYang, China) and visualized under UV or by staining with potassium permanganate. Blue LEDs strips (maximum emission at 470 nm, 36 W, distance ca. 2cm) were used to irradiate the reaction mixtures, which were bought from Colour-LED-Luminance (Taobao). Column chromatography was carried out on Silica Gel 200-300 mesh (Macklin, China). Melting points were determined using a Yanaco micro melting point apparatus Model MP-500D. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra were recorded using Bruker Ascend 500 spectrometer (FT, 500 MHz for { } ^ { 1 } \mathrm { H } , 126 MHz for ^ { 1 3 } \mathrm { C } ) . The following residual solvent signals were used as references for ^ 1 \mathrm { H } and ^ { 1 3 } \mathrm { C } NMR spectra: CDCl<sub>3</sub>, \delta _ { \mathrm { H } } 7.26 ppm, δ<sub>C</sub> 77.16 ppm; { \mathrm { D M S O } } – d _ { 6 } , δ<sub>H</sub> 2.50 ppm, δ<sub>C</sub> 39.52 ppm, \delta _ { \mathrm { C } } was calibrated using absolute referencing to the ^ 1 \mathrm { H } spectrum). Coupling constants (J) are reported in Hertz (Hz) to the nearest 0.1 Hz. Multiplicities are reported using the following abbreviations: s = singlet, d = doublet, t = triplet, q = quartet, m = multiplet, br = broad resonance. High-resolution mass spectra (HR-MS) for new compounds were recorded on the FTMS Bruker Solarix QTOF spectrometer in electrospray ionization (ESI<sup>+</sup>/ESI<sup>-</sup>) mode. Ultraviolet-visible (UV-vis) spectra were recorded by the Hitachi UV Spectrophotometer U-3900H.
